concept.name: Paper trading
concept.definition: Running a strategy against live or delayed market data with simulated orders and account balances instead of real executions and capital.
concept.intuition: It is part of the machinery that converts strategy instructions into simulated positions, cash flows, and performance.
concept.mechanics: Submit orders to a simulated brokerage model, record assumed fills, fees, and buying power, and reconcile those assumptions with observable markets.
concept.failure_modes: Simplified timing, liquidity, fee, borrow, funding, or corporate-action assumptions can make simulated results unattainable live.
concept.misconceptions: A detailed simulator reduces modeling error but cannot reproduce every queue event or future market condition.
concept.example: A paper account buys 100 shares, but its immediate full fill is flagged as optimistic because only 20 shares were displayed.
